title: After the release every QuickBooks location has four empty category rows
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use the production test account.
  • Use a location connected to QuickBooks Online before the release.
  • Before the release, note the rows and their accounts on this location's ShopView Accounts page.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The QuickBooks page opens.

Step 2:

  • Four category rows show under Cost of Parts, each empty, with no hint while the setting is off; the other rows and their accounts are the ones noted before the release.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-12295 (Story 13, Release day, seeding and migration)

  • S13-R2: “The same migration creates one empty ShopView Accounts row per category at every location with a connected QuickBooks company (S5-R5); the rows carry no hint while the setting is off. A location connected later gets its rows when the connection is made, as other rows do.”
  • S13-R5: “Verification after the run, per organization: four categories, four QuickBooks rows per connected location, four hub mappings populated (Comeback included), the setting off. The rule-zero verify of S9-R14 runs the same day. If engineering ships the feature behind a deploy switch until launch day, the switch is removed with the launch and is not a product setting (Key Decisions, No feature flag).”
  • S5-R5: “The rows are shown whether or not the Internal Work Orders setting is on, so the accountant can map ahead of time.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - needs records and figures noted on production before the release reaches production; run on production after the release
